title: Pete Sessions Apple Stock Sale: $100K–$250K (Congress Trade, Sep 2026)
content:
Rep. Pete Sessions (TX-17) disclosed a sale of $100,001–$250,000 of Apple (AAPL) stock dated September 22, 2026.

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

What's been disclosed

  • The sale: A sale of Apple stock worth $100,001–$250,000 on September 22, disclosed the same day.
  • Price since: Bargo's estimate puts Apple about 1.8% lower on October 2 than on the sale date.
  • Other trades in the same member's filings: On September 14 he also sold Alphabet ($15,001–$50,000) and AbbVie ($15,001–$50,000), disclosed September 18.

Quick FAQ

When do members of Congress have to disclose their trades?
Under the STOCK Act, within 45 days of the transaction. This sale was disclosed the same day; across the 100 most recent trade lines we pulled, the average gap between trade and disclosure was about three weeks.

Why is the amount a range?
Filings report value bands such as $100,001–$250,000 instead of exact dollar amounts.

Where does the price comparison come from?
It is Bargo's estimate, comparing the price on the transaction date with the October 2 price. It is not the member's actual execution price.
